plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like composite flower heads made up of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disk. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and the plant is grown widely for seeds, oil, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across the United States, Europe, Ukraine, Russia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west in a process called heliotropism, but mature flower heads stop moving and typically face east.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a favorite of bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer, peaking from July to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the western Mediterranean; widely cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the Pacific Northwest of the United States
plants.funFact: Lavender oil has been used since ancient Roman times, and the plant's name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Epilobium angustifolium
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower that forms spires of bright magenta-pink flowers which open from the bottom up. It is among the first plants to colonize burned or cleared land, and it carpets mountain meadows and forest clearings.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September)
plants.location: Circumpolar in the Northern Hemisphere, including Alaska, Canada, Scandinavia, Siberia, and northern Europe
plants.funFact: Locals say that when fireweed blooms reach the top of the stalk, summer is nearly over, since the flowers open progressively from bottom to top.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large, round leaves that rise above the water and stunning, fragrant flowers on tall stalks. The leaves have a self-cleaning, water-repellent surface, and the flowers are central to many cultural and religious traditions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, from June to September in monsoon and temperate Asia
plants.location: Native to Asia and northern Australia; cultivated in ponds across India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and the southern United States
plants.funFact: Lotus flowers can regulate their own temperature, staying around 30–35°C even when the air is much cooler, which helps attract pollinating beetles.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the genus, made of showy pink bracts surrounding a central cone of tiny flowers. It is South Africa's national flower and a popular cut flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from late summer through early spring depending on the variety
plants.location: Native to the fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape in South Africa
plants.funFact: Proteas are an ancient plant family that dates back about 300 million years, and the genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change his shape.
